{{Quote|We should not have made this bargain.|Rune Haako|<ref name="tpm" />}}
'''Rune Haako''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] and the [[Settlement Officer/Legends|Settlement Officer]] of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], as well as a [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] to [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] in the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] leading up to and through the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. He replaced [[Hath Monchar]] as Gunray's second-in-command not long after the [[Eriadu Trade Summit]], and disapproved of his superior's fraternization with the clandestine [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]], [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]]. Around this [[Time/Legends|time]], Gunray and Haako had to deal with the desertion of Monchar, who, it was believed, would leak Federation secrets. Upon Haako's recommendation, Gunray hired the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Mahwi Lihnn]] to hunt down and [[Death/Legends|kill]] Monchar. Eventually, both Monchar and Lihnn were killed by one of Sidious's agents, [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]]. In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], Haako served as [[Advisor/Legends|advisor]] to Gunray when the Viceroy brought about the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Blockade of Naboo]]&mdash;the Trade Federation's way of protesting the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate's]] new taxation of trade routes. Tensions escalated when the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Mission to Naboo|dispatched]] two [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] to negotiate with the Federation, which ultimately brought about the Invasion of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].

Naboo's monarch, [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Amidala]], and the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] in turn, were able to [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|break]] the Federation's occupation, and as a result both Gunray and Haako were arrested. The pair evaded any significant punishment due to the Federation's still-considerable influence, and were able to return to their offices within the Federation. Ultimately, the Federation joined [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku's]] separatist movement, the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], which aimed to break away from the Galactic Republic altogether. Haako continued to serve as Gunray's lieutenant, and the Viceroy became a key figure on the Confederacy's [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]]. Ten years after the failed Naboo blockade, in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Haako and Gunray were present on [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]] when now-[[Senator/Legends|Senator]] Amidala, along with two Jedi Knights, were arrested by Confederate agents and sentenced to death. In turn, the Confederacy's actions provoked an [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|invasion]] of the planet by the Galactic Republic, sparking the beginning of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Over the next three years, Haako and Gunray continued to serve the Confederacy, as they were shipped from system to system in order to evade the clutches of the Galactic Republic. They were kept under the protection of one of Dooku's [[General/Legends|generals]], [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], and by [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the Council sought refuge on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]]. As the Clone Wars drew to a close, Haako, Gunray, and the other Separatist leaders were summarily assassinated by another agent of Sidious's, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]].

==Biography==
===Early career===
{{Quote|One ship and a treasure box. If our benefactor really is who he claims to be, such losses are meaningless. And if he is, he is a thing to fear, not to delight. And how can we be certain, in any case? What proof does he offer, Viceroy?|Rune Haako|<ref name="cod" />}}
In the final decades of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], Rune Haako was employed by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], as a legal [[Advisor/Legends|advisor]]<ref name="TPMV">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>&mdash;or ''cohorta'' in [[Pak Pak/Legends|Pak Pak]]<ref name="GPBTG">[[Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide (real-life book)|''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'']]</ref>&mdash;to [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]]. When Gunray decided to ally himself with [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] in order to further his position in the Federation, Haako expressed his grave concern. There was no proof of Sidious' power, to Haako's mind, although during a holo-conference, he suspected that the shadowy [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] had connections in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]. Sidious ordered Gunray to commission a droid army, in spite of [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum's]] threatened taxation of trade routes. Simultaneously, Sidious arranged the deaths of the [[Trade Federation Directorate]] at the [[Eriadu Trade Summit]], allowing Gunray and his allies to assume control of the organization. Meanwhile, Haako helped oversee the formation of the new droid army, negotiating and dealing with the various contractors, while still holding his reservations about the goings on.<ref name="cod" />

Haako was promoted to his position after fellow Neimoidian [[Hath Monchar]] betrayed the Trade Federation. In the hopes of preventing Monchar from betraying any Federation secrets, Haako suggested that Gunray enlist the services of hunter [[Mahwi Lihnn]] to [[Skirmish on Coruscant (32 BBY)|reel him in]]. Monchar was eventually slain by Sidious' apprentice, [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], who also felled Lihnn, much to the concern of the Neimoidians.<ref name="sh">''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]''</ref> Following the incident Haako served as the Trade Federation Settlement Officer, meaning that his primary duties were to act as a diplomatic attaché and legal counsel to the viceroy. He was widely known for his jurisprudential acumen, but when confronted with real threats, he reacted with the sort of pessimism that was typical of his species.<ref name="db" /> Despite this, he would still be called upon to lend an air of credibility to any of the Trade Federation's more dubious activities, due to his skill as a manipulator.<ref name="cswe">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

===Invasion of Naboo===
{{Quote|Captain, we've searched the ship and there is no trace of the Jedi. They may have gotten on one of your landing craft.''"<br />"''If they're down here, sir, we'll find them.|Rune Haako and OOM-9|<ref name="tpm" />}}
[[File:RuneHaako_ep1ig.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Haako in 32 BBY.]]
In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="32 BBY">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of {{Film|I}} to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].</ref> Haako was at Viceroy Nute Gunray's side when the Trade Federation decided to blockade the peaceful [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of Naboo, as a response to the taxation of certain trade routes. He was one of the few people, besides Gunray and [[Daultay Dofine/Legends|Daultay Dofine]], who knew that Darth Sidious was the one who had devised the idea of the blockade. Haako was, like Gunray, cautious of Sidious, and later lamented his superior's choice to "bargain" with the Sith Lord. When the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Mission to Naboo|dispatched]] two [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] ambassadors, [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], to settle the dispute, Gunray panicked when they arrived on his [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] at the time, the [[Saak'ak/Legends|''Saak'ak'']], and contacted Sidious via [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]]. Much to the Neimoidian's surprise, Sidious ordered the execution of the Jedi and the commencement of the invasion of Naboo. Gunray dispatched a squad of [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]] to kill the Jedi even as he filled their waiting room with [[Dioxis/Legends|Dioxis]] gas and had their [[Consular-class light cruiser/Legends|''Consular''-class cruiser]], the [[Radiant VII/Legends|''Radiant VII'']], destroyed; these were actions that, as Haako predicted, would prove to be ineffective. Haako was not surprised when the Jedi survived Gunray's assassination attempts which included sending [[Droideka/Legends|droidekas]] after the Jedi, and proceeded to inadvertently remind Gunray of his encounters with them during the [[Stark Hyperspace War/Legends|Stark Hyperspace War]].<ref name="tpm" /><ref name="Star Wars: Republic: The Stark Hyperspace War">''[[Star Wars: The Stark Hyperspace War]]''</ref>

Gunray was then contacted by [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Amidala]], who assured Gunray that the blockade would not last much longer. Haako was fearful that she suspected the impending [[Capture of Theed/Legends|attack]], and suspected that she might try to contact [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Gunray promptly ordered [[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9]], the invasion forces' [[OOM command battle droid/Legends|commander]], to attack the small towns of [[New Centrif]], [[Parrlay]], and [[Vis/Legends|Vis]]. The attacks disrupted all interplanetary communications to and from Naboo.<ref name="gb">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref>

Shortly thereafter, OOM-9 won the First Battle of Theed and captured the Queen. Gunray and Haako visited the [[Theed Royal Palace/Legends|Theed Royal Palace]], savoring their victory. Upon their return to the ''Saak'ak'', the two officers received news that the Queen had escaped the planet with the aid of the Jedi that they had earlier failed to destroy. This failure incurred the wrath of Sidious, who appeared to be extremely displeased. Sidious revealed his apprentice, [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], the killer of Haako's predecessor, Hath Monchar. Sidious assured Gunray and Haako that Maul would find their "lost ship". Whether or not the sight of Maul was meant to be a veiled threat or if it was perceived as such, Gunray and Haako were both badly shaken. When the holo-conference was over, Haako expressed his fears about their alliance with the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] to Gunray.<ref name="tpm" />

[[File:HaakoGunrayPalpy-Ep1.png|thumb|right|200px|Rune Haako with Nute Gunray and Darth Sidious's hologram on Naboo in the Theed Royal Palace.]]
The Neimoidians then moved to the Royal Palace, making it their permanent residence during the occupation of the planet. Gunray ordered OOM-9 to eliminate the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] that he had heard rumors about, in order to more fully and effectively control the planet. With the help of Darth Maul, Federation forces attacked and routed the [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]] at [[Lake Paonga/Legends|Lake Paonga]]. However, OOM-9 only partially completed his goal, an oversight that would soon come back to haunt Haako and the Federation.<ref name="gb" />

====Defeat on Naboo and arrest====
{{Quote|Meanwhile, the Queen had invaded the palace. She tricked Rune and Nute by using a decoy. Just remembering this makes me feel weary. I could always count on Neimoidian stupidity, but usually it worked to my advantage.|Darth Sidious|<ref name="Star Wars Episode I Journal: Darth Maul">''[[Star Wars Journal: Darth Maul]]''</ref>}}
The Queen eventually returned to Naboo, a move that not only surprised Haako and Gunray, but Sidious as well (as the Sith Lord, at least, led them to believe). OOM-9 and Darth Maul's previous attempts to destroy the Gungans had obviously not been a total success, as the Queen contacted the survivors and raised a Gungan army to fight back. Through an elaborate plan, she was able to have the droid armies deactivated, and Gunray and Haako captured, in a stunning reverse-''coup d'etat ''in which she used her decoy-handmaiden [[Sabé/Legends|Sabé]] at the last moment to help her accomplish that.<ref name="tpm" /><ref name="Star Wars Journal: Queen Amidala">''[[Star Wars Journal: Queen Amidala]]''</ref><ref name="Star Wars Episode I Journal: Darth Maul" /> When the Battle of Naboo was concluded, Haako was formally arrested along with Gunray, and the two were transported to Coruscant for trial.<ref name="cswe" /> After several trials, however, Gunray was never formally punished for the Naboo incident and maintained control over the Trade Federation,<ref name="aotc">{{Film|II}}</ref> and due to the Federation's still-considerable power, Haako much like Gunray was able to avoid any real punishment.<ref name="cswe" />

===Clone Wars===
{{Quote|Our purse worlds now belong to the Republic. Our only hope is to find sanctuary in the Outer Rim. Otherwise, this ship will have to serve as our home&mdash;and perhaps our final resting place!|Rune Haako|<ref name="loe">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref>}}
Haako would later serve at Gunray's side within the leadership of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] throughout the Clone Wars. He accompanied Gunray to the Separatist summit on Geonosis, and viewed the opening stages of the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]] directly from [[Petranaki arena]], when an army of [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] and Republic [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] invaded the planet. Retreating with Gunray into the CIS war room, Haako advised the Viceroy that they should flee the planet. The pair then escaped aboard Gunray's shuttle, ''[[Lapiz Cutter/Legends|Lapiz Cutter]]'', to the orbiting Federation fleet.<ref name="aotc" />

[[File:Haako_on_Geonosis.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Haako, Gunray, and Dooku on Geonosis.]]
After the Battle of Geonosis, Haako continued to follow Gunray everywhere, and was present with the viceroy in [[Koto-Si/Legends|Koto-Si]] on [[Neimoidia/Legends|Neimoidia]].<ref name="hn">{{InsiderCite|71|CIS Shadowfeed Dispatch 14:10:05 Edition}}</ref> In the later stages of the war, Haako, along with Gunray, was caught up in the [[Siege of Cato Neimoidia|Battle of Cato Neimoidia]]. In the panic of evacuating their homeworld, they left behind the [[Mechno-chair/Legends|mechno-chair]], which had been equipped with a [[Holotransmitter/Legends|holotransceiver]] that contained the communications signals and codes that was used by Darth Sidious to communicate via hologram to Viceroy Gunray. The pair lived in constant fear that [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] would find out, as they were shuttled, along with the rest of the Separatist Council, from safeworld to safeworld. Although at first, they were able to keep the loss of the mechno-chair a secret, Grievous soon found out. Despite the fact that the general was livid, both Neimoidians escaped his wrath alive.<ref name="loe" />

===Death===
{{Quote|Stop! No!|Haako's last words|<ref name="rots" />}}
[[File:Haako_pray_for_mercy_from_vader.jpg|thumb|250px|Haako begs for mercy from Darth Vader, moments before his death.]]
After General Grievous's failed attempts to capture the Supreme Chancellor at Coruscant as well as the death of Dooku, the Separatists began to retreat to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]. They were first moved to [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]], where they were kept in check by Grievous, now Head of State of the CIS. Sidious, through Grievous, then ordered the Separatist Council to relocate to [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]]. Haako and the other Separatist leaders were sent to the lava planet to orchestrate their armies' operations and eventual shutdown from there.<ref name="rots" />

When Grievous was killed on Utapau by General Kenobi, the very same Jedi who had been a thorn in the Federation's side thirteen years prior, Gunray became the ''de facto'' head of the CIS. Sidious contacted Gunray one final time, assuring him and the rest of the Council that they would be "taken care of" by his new apprentice. When [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] was sent to [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|kill the Separatist leaders]] on Mustafar, Rune Haako was present and futilely demanded that Vader stop the slaughter. As Vader killed [[Poggle the Lesser/Legends|Poggle the Lesser]], [[Aruteous Gunnay|Rute Gunnay]] and others, Haako escaped to the conference room of the bunker with Techno Union foreman Wat Tambor. Haako attempted to hide, but Vader strode in and ended the Neimoidian's life with a single slash across the chest before proceeding to kill Tambor and Gunray, destroying the Confederacy of Independent Systems.<ref name="rots" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|I want droidekas up here at once!''"<br />"''We will not survive this.|Nute Gunray and Rune Haako|<ref name="tpm" />}}
[[File:Haakmiester2.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Rune Haako was a skilled manipulator.]]
In many ways, Haako was a typical Neimoidian&mdash;constantly paranoid and devoutly greedy. He was less brash than his superior, Nute Gunray, who would often jump to conclusions and act without thinking. Haako's advice would often help avoid or save a "situation" from occurring or getting out of hand, and his constant warnings helped keep Gunray in check. Haako was also persistently pessimistic and ever wary of the Sith, possibly more so than Gunray.<ref name="tpm" /> It was possible that Haako's personality grated on Sidious, who always looked forward to the day that he could be rid of the Neimoidians.<ref name="sh" /> His wariness and pessimism could be mistaken for typical Neimoidian cowardice but in all likelihood it was more cautiousness and common sense of Haako's part as by the end of the Clone Wars, he courageously tried to order Vader to stop his massacre of the Separatist leaders, rather than blubber mercy pleas like most of the other council members.<ref name="rots" />

Haako was also known to be a skilled manipulator, who was at his best when sitting at a conference table conducting negotiations. This was more than likely why Gunray trusted his advice when dealing with the stubborn Queen Amidala. It was not known whether Haako had any political ambitions of his own.<ref name="db" /> At some stage in his early life, Haako was struck with [[palsy]]. It effectively crippled his left arm and leg, leaving them virtually useless. Haako would continue to limp until 32 BBY, but the ailment was clearly gone by 22 BBY.<ref name="cod" /><ref name="tpm" /><ref name="aotc" />

==Equipment==
Haako used a poison-tipped knife as a weapon.<ref name="H2H" /> During the blockade of Naboo in 32 BBY,<ref name="32 BBY" /> Haako wore a sumptuous [[Clothing/Legends|robe]] made from expensive cloth and an [[attorney's cowl]].<ref name="SWCE">''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref> Near the end of the Clone Wars in 19 BBY,<ref name="19 BBY">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of {{Film|III}} to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].</ref> the Neimoidian wore a heritage miter and dark blue robes with a [[Cato Neimoidian yoke collar/Legends|Cato Neimoidian yoke collar]].<ref name="cvd" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Rune_Haako_Concept_Art.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Concept art of Rune Haako]]
Rune Haako was played by [[Jerome Blake]] and voiced by [[James Taylor (voice actor)|James Taylor]] in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="tpm" /> In [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']], he was played by [[Alan Ruscoe]]<ref name="aotc" /> and voiced by [[Christopher Truswell]]{{Fact}} (despite the credits identifying him as [[Lott Dod/Legends|Lott Dod]]),<ref name="aotc" /> and played by [[Sandy Thompson]] in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']].<ref name="rots" /> He was voiced by [[Hamilton Camp]] in the game ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''.<ref name="gb" />

Throughout the several ''Revenge of the Sith'' adaptations, Haako's death was depicted differently. In the [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (video game)|''Revenge of the Sith'' video game]], Rune Haako dies when he is cornered by Vader. "I am asking you for mercy," he pleaded. "You won't kill me. It's not allowed for a Jedi Knight." Vader replied, "There is much you fail to understand," before killing him.<ref name="rotsg">[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' video game]]</ref> In the [[Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith (comic series)|''Revenge of the Sith'' comic adaptation]], Haako appears in his ''Phantom Menace'' costume, unlike in the film.<ref name="rotsc">[[Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith (comic series)|''Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith'' comic adaptation]]</ref> In the [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|novelization of ''Revenge of the Sith'']], Rune Haako falls over and attempts to scurry away from Vader, surrendering and saying that its not allowed for a Jedi to kill an unarmed enemy. Vader casually replies "''You fought a war to destroy the Jedi, congratulations on your success''" before stabbing Haako through the face.

Haako's death is never shown on screen; however, [[Ben Burtt]]'s editing places another character's death right after we see him on camera, leading us to believe it was him dying at that particular moment. We do see him saying "Stop, No!" (that was definitely him) but right after that the editing cuts to another character being struck down. That character was [[Aruteous Gunnay]]. Haako's body can later be found in the conference room.<ref name="rots" /> ''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]'' erroneously labels a picture of [[Aito Laff]] as Rune Haako.

===Confusion over ''Attack of the Clones'' appearance===
[[File:RuneHaako-AOTC.jpg|thumb|Haako in ''Attack of the Clones'']]
Rune Haako's mask was lost shortly after ''The Phantom Menace'' finished filming. The production crew gave [[Daultay Dofine/Legends|Daultay Dofine's]] mask to Alan Ruscoe instead, and for a time it was thought that this "new" Neimoidian would become a separate character, and he was given the name [[Gilramos Libkath]], after [[Gillian Libbert]] and [[Kathryn Ramos]].<ref name="hcb">{{Blog|holocron|29|Mistaken Identities}}</ref> However, despite being called Gilramos Libkath in ''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''<ref name="aotcvd">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> and being credited as Lott Dod in the credits of the movie,<ref name="aotc" /> the official [[Lucasfilm|LFL]] explanation, as stated by [[Leland Chee]], is that it is in fact Haako,<ref name="hcb" /> despite his different appearance and much deeper voice than in ''The Phantom Menace''<ref name="tpm" /> and ''Revenge of the Sith''.<ref name="rots" /> ''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]'' also establishes Haako being at Geonosis, not Libkath.<ref name="cvd">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> However, this did not stop Libkath from being established as a different character that looks and dresses similar to Haako in ''Attack of the Clones''.<ref name="aotc" /> To add to the confusion, the official site's [[Databank (original)|Databank]] claims that Haako appears in only Episodes I and III, supporting the Libkath theory.<ref name="db" />

It should also be noted that the ''Attack of the Clones'' Neimoidian wears a purple drape similar to the supreme representative mantle worn by [[Lott Dod/Legends|Lott Dod]] in ''The Phantom Menace''. Since there is no mention of Haako becoming a Senator between the two movies (and lacks the garb in ''Revenge of the Sith''), this would appear to support the "Lott Dod with a facelift" theory.<ref name="aotc" />
